Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

HI Sarah it's Francis. I have a situation with my ThorP2 I received it a
couple weeks ago. Lately the miner stops mining on my web ui and my node. I
have to reset the miner every other day or once a day. Please advise. Thank
you! Francis
Handed to the team · Hardware fault question beyond product facts, needs JD.

Hi Francis,

Sorry to hear that. A miner that drops off every day or two is most often running older firmware, so start there. Open the Harlo OS dashboard on the unit, note the version it shows, and compare it with the latest release for the Thor P2 at https://harlolabs.com. If you are behind, update first, as an older build is the most common cause of these dropouts.

If it is already current, the next suspects are power and network. Make sure it is on the supplied PSU on its own outlet, not sharing a strip, and try the unit on a wired connection or closer to the router, since a weak signal can look like the miner stopping.

I have also passed this to JD, who handles our hardware. He picks it up today at 10am ET and will reply to you here. If you want an answer sooner, he is most active on our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post in the server and mention @nullhashrate. When you write, include your Harlo OS version, the pool you are mining to, and whether the unit goes fully dark or just stops hashing. One more thing we have to ask, has the unit been overclocked at any point, as that changes what we can do on warranty.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

Hi yes all is up to date, it also hashes no greater than 9.7ths and power
is only 135 watts. It is on its own and close to the router. None of my
other miners(15) have an issue. I also noticed today that when I picked up
the power supply it sounded like something is loose inside. Thank you
Francis
Handed to the team · Looks like a failing PSU, needs JD to confirm and a PSU-only replacement rather

Hi Francis,

That rattle changes the picture. Low power draw, hashrate stuck under spec and a daily dropout all point at the power supply rather than the miner, and a loose part inside the PSU fits that exactly. Please stop using it for now, as a failing supply can take the board with it.

The good news is you do not have to send the whole unit back. We do PSU only replacements. Fill in the RMA intake form here and say in the notes that it is the power supply on a Thor P2 that rattles and reads around 135 watts: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12t6skK21Qb8GfAdUQ9nOhJ1tVINJ60T3AIAsyhBwnYM/viewform

One thing I have to ask for the record, has the unit ever been overclocked or had its firmware modified, as that affects warranty cover. If it has been running stock, you are covered.

I have passed the details to JD, who handles our hardware, and he picks this up today at 10am ET and will reply to you here. If you want him faster, he is very active on our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post in the server and mention @nullhashrate.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

Only what you have sent to me. It's running all stock settings that you
have put on the miner. Ok Thank you

Hi Francis,

That is what I wanted to hear. Running stock, it is fully covered under warranty, so nothing stands in the way of a replacement.

Go ahead and fill in the RMA form whenever you get a moment, with a note that it is the power supply on a Thor P2 that rattles and reads around 135 watts, and that the unit has only ever run stock. That is the only intake we use, and it gets you a prepaid return label. Processing takes up to 10 days once the part reaches the warehouse.

Keep the miner powered off until the new supply arrives, just to protect the board.

JD has the details on his side too, so if he sees anything in your numbers that points elsewhere, he will come back to you here.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support
